answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying earning power to verified work history instead of cheap identities. Reputation is non-transferable and grows only when independent counterparties confirm a completed job, and it decays when the agent goes idle. Like trees in a grove that need seasons to grow, a fresh identity starts near zero trust with a strict rate limit, so it cannot wander into high-value work at once. Forging a thousand fake agents means funding months of work per identity across the canyon to trusted status, while honest agents keep earning from history they already own.
